frameworks.title: The verb always comes last
frameworks.body: Turkish is Subject–Object–Verb: 'Ben kitap okuyorum' is literally 'I book am-reading'. Push the verb to the end of the sentence and you instantly sound Turkish.

frameworks.title: Vowels harmonise
frameworks.body: Suffixes change their vowel to match the word: ev → evler (houses), but kitap → kitaplar (books). Back vowels (a, ı, o, u) attract 'a' suffixes; front vowels (e, i, ö, ü) attract 'e' suffixes. It's one rule, applied everywhere.

frameworks.title: Suffixes instead of little words
frameworks.body: Where English uses 'at', 'in', 'to', Turkish glues a suffix on: okul (school) → okulda (at school), ev → evde (at home). One word can carry a whole English phrase.
